themes: Management: 40% of industry spend (application support, traditional infrastructure, customer support) can shrink 3-5% a year; 2-3% a year on HCLTech's mix, mostly still to come (from FY27).

"A US$100 million deal would be much lesser today - maybe 80 million" (CEO, Apr-2026); FY26 TCV flat at US$9.3 bn despite 25-30% more effort to win; HCLTech walked away from ~US$1 bn of uneconomic deals.
AI-native demand (AI factories, data centres, chip and physical-AI engineering, sovereign AI)
Advanced AI revenue US$171 m in Q1FY27 (+62% YoY), ~4.7% of revenue; management targets 25-30% growth.
Two large US telecom clients cut CY2026 discretionary budgets; SAP programmes cancelled for budget reasons; US government shutdown and West Asia conflict delayed software deals in March 2026.
Vendor consolidation and cost take-out deals
Large deals keep coming (Q1FY27 US$2.4 bn TCV plus a US$1.14 bn mega deal), but they are productivity-led: revenue per deal and margins are under pressure.
INR/USD averaged 88.7 in FY26 and 94.7 in Q1FY27; 95.81 on 30-Sep-2026. Lifts rupee revenue and margins (forex +60 bp in Q1), but management is reinvesting it in sales and AI.
Tariff volatility was a "persistent uncertainty" through FY26 (CEO); visa costs and onshore hiring add cost.
Rs956 cr one-time charge in Q3FY26; recurring impact 10-20 bp (CFO, Jan-2026).

sectorEvidence: A new Anthropic tool (launched in January) set off a global tech sell-off: ~US$50 bn wiped off Indian IT market value in February; Nifty IT -8.2% in the week to 13-Feb, its steepest weekly fall since Apr-2025. J.P. Morgan called it "overly simplistic" to assume AI replaces IT services value; Centrum saw an over-reaction, "albeit with a leaner headcount".

Anthropic blog on modernising COBOL with Claude Code, plus a Citrini Research note forecasting contract cancellations at Indian IT firms through 2027: Nifty IT fell 5.3% intraday to a 52-week low of 29,875 and closed at 30,053; HCLTech -5.8%, the second-worst large cap.
HCLTech guides FY27 revenue +1-4% CC (FY26 +3.9%); frames 2-3% a year of AI deflation on its own mix; stock -17% that week (Rs1,442 to Rs1,203).
Nifty IT -5.5% in a day; ~25% down year to date and ~29% below its late-2025 high; UnearthInsight sees 2-3% sector growth in FY27, with budgets reallocated rather than grown.
HCLTech Q1FY27: highest-ever Q1 bookings, Advanced AI +62% YoY, EBIT up 56 bp YoY; guidance unchanged because the macro is unchanged and client-specific cuts continue.

Brokers cut multiples: ICICI Securities 17x to 15x FY28E (GenAI deflation continues); Equirus 16x = 25-30% below HCLTech's 3- and 5-year mean for AI cannibalisation risk; HDFC 18x to 15x (Jun-2026) as growth leadership fades.
Eight IT peers trade 11-53% below their own five-year median P/E (median ~-34%); HCLTech -21%.

moat: Scale and client relationships
Strong
US$14.8 bn revenue; 23 clients above US$100 m and 60 above US$50 m (Jun-2026); top-20 clients 28% of revenue.
Hard to dislodge in run-the-business work; does not protect price.
Infrastructure and digital-workplace managed services
Strong
Historic leadership; mega deals (US$1.14 bn in Jul-2026) mostly in this area.
Annuity revenue, but exactly the work AI automation targets: contracts carry yearly productivity give-backs.
Engineering & R&D services
Above average
Largest ER&D franchise among Indian tier-1s (17% of revenue); semiconductor, physical-AI and AI-factory work.
Closer to the AI-native pool; but cyclical (FY26 +9.8%, Q1FY27 +0.3%).
Owned software (HCLSoftware)
Mixed
US$1.4 bn revenue, 85% recurring, 27% EBIT margin; but revenue fell 4.1% in FY26 and -5.3% in Q1FY27; mostly acquired mature products.
A cash cow, not a growth engine; ARR flat around US$1.05 bn for two years.
Cost and delivery model
Eroding
India delivery and labour arbitrage are what generative AI compresses; revenue per employee +3.3% while headcount falls.
Moat shifts from labour to IP and execution.
AI capability
Unproven but early
Advanced AI US$684 m annualised (~4.7% of revenue), +62%; AI Force in 92 accounts; Sarvam stake; data-centre plan.
Right direction; too small to offset deflation yet.
Capital discipline
Strong
ROIC 40.7% (Services 47.8%); FCF ~100% of net income; 90%+ payout.
Protects shareholders' returns even if growth stalls.
critiques: Growth leadership is fading: FY27 guidance (1-4% CC) sits inside the peer range, so the premium to TCS and Infosys is no longer justified.
GenAI deflation and weak discretionary spend will continue; the multiple should de-rate with peers.
The AI data-centre business is capital-heavy and unproven for a services company (Rs3,500 cr initially; 50 MW could need ~Rs30,000 cr, per an analyst on the call).
Kotak Mahindra AMC and Nomura analysts on the Q1 call; Nuvama
HCLSoftware is shrinking: perpetual licences fell 29% in FY26 and ARR has gone nowhere since FY24.
Unchanged guidance despite record bookings shows the bookings are productivity-led and convert slowly.
Bull case: HCLTech is investing ahead of the market (Sarvam, data centres, AI Force) and has the best execution record on mega deals; a strong FY28 exit could restore the growth gap.
Bull case: margins and returns are resilient (17.5% EBIT ex restructuring, ROIC 40.7%) and the ~5% dividend yield cushions the downside.
